title: What Makes a Redriver Smart?
summary: Learn about the features that make Aries and Taurus Smart Redrivers intelligent. Temperature compensation, eye monitoring, mid-frequency boost, and more.
body_markdown:
As AI systems scale and technology accelerates, higher data rates, denser backplanes, longer copper channels, and increasingly dynamic workloads are making it harder to maintain reliable links across every board, connector, and cable in the system. Hyperscalers and AI infrastructure providers must simultaneously close channels, optimize power budgets, and keep all links healthy as temperature, channel conditions, and system behavior change.


[Changes to modulation, data rates, and system level requirements](https://www.asteralabs.com/resources/blog/nothing-out-of-reach-the-aries-pcie-7-family-delivers-copper-and-optical-signal-conditioning-for-ais-next-chapter/) create a new set of use cases that can be addressed with redrivers rather than with full signal regeneration via retimers. However, redrivers have conventionally been transparent analog devices that simply apply a fixed equalization response and pass the signal through. Traditional redrivers could not observe the channel, adapt to changing conditions, or provide much insight when a link begins to degrade.


To make low-latency, low-power signal compensation viable for deployment at AI hyperscalers, Astera Labs has introduced a new class of Smart Redrivers in both our[Taurus](https://www.asteralabs.com/products/taurus-smart-signal-conditioners/) and[Aries](https://www.asteralabs.com/products/aries-smart-redrivers/) product families. Smart Redrivers are purpose-built with the link intelligence needed to monitor, tune, and manage high-speed links in real-time.


## What Is a Smart Redriver?


A Smart Redriver does more than compensate for channel loss. It provides system engineers with visibility into link health and the ability to respond to changing conditions before a marginal link becomes a failure. Fleet-wide total visibility is essential for modern AI deployments where any at-risk link or failure must be identified instantly with pinpoint precision to maintain uptime.


Smart redrivers approach this in two complementary ways: mission mode, which provides continuous visibility and tuning for active systems running live traffic, and monitoring mode, which provides deeper channel diagnostics during validation, manufacturing, and troubleshooting.


## Mission Mode: Keeping Live Links Healthy in Real Time


Continuous visibility helps systems operate reliably under the stress of live AI workload traffic. Mission mode provides granular live telemetry data that maximizes uptime for Smart Redrivers in hyperscale deployments.


#### Detecting Signal Integrity Problems Before Links Fail


A traditional redriver does not monitor the channel. If the signal is over-equalized, operating beyond the linear region, or falling below a valid signal level, the system may receive little or no warning before errors, recoveries, or link loss occur.


Smart Redrivers use signal intelligence to detect these conditions. Peak detection and loss-of-linearity detection allow the device to monitor signal behavior continuously. When the signal indicates an over-boost or over-drive condition, the device can generate a real-time firmware flag.


Smart Redrivers also support loss-of-signal detection, providing systems with an indication that the link is down or that an event such as surprise removal may have occurred.


This visibility changes the way teams debug connectivity. Instead of discovering a problem only after a link has failed, engineers can use device-level indicators to isolate whether an emerging issue is related to signal margin, channel behavior, or a system event.


#### Compensating for Temperature-Dependent Channel Loss


High-speed channels do not behave the same way across all operating conditions. Passive channel loss and redriver boost can both change as temperature rises, reducing margin and increasing the risk of bit errors, link recovery events, and link drops.


A one-time equalization setting cannot account for every operating condition. At elevated temperatures, changes in device and channel characteristics can reduce effective boost and signal margin. Smart Redrivers use temperature-compensated equalization to help maintain channel performance. As the device detects changes in temperature, it can automatically adjust the EQ setting to counteract the associated change in channel behavior, resulting in stable performance across different operating conditions.


This results in more stable links across thermal conditions, with temperature variances treatable with device-level precision rather than board-level tuning.


#### Shaping the EQ Curve for the Actual Channel


Different channels can have very different loss profiles. A PCB trace, a twinax assembly, and a channel that combines both may each introduce different amounts of loss at different frequencies depending on the medium the signal travels through.


Traditional redrivers typically focus on equalization around the Nyquist frequency. That approach may leave a mid-frequency dip in the channel response, creating a non-flat response at the receiver.


Smart Redrivers add programmable mid-frequency boost, with an independent adjustment range of approximately 2 to 8 dB at 10 GHz. As a result, the EQ curve can be shaped around the actual loss characteristics of the channel.


For system designers, that flexibility can make it easier to close the link budget across a wider range of board materials, connector paths, and cable configurations.


#### Remaining Transparent to the Protocol


Signal intelligence should not require a redriver to take over link-training. Both Aries and Taurus Smart Redrivers are designed to remain protocol-transparent while preserving the pre-shoot and de-emphasis characteristics of the incoming signal.


Aries PCIe® Smart Redrivers are transparent to PCIe equalization phases 0 through 3. Taurus Smart Redrivers remain transparent to the training process for Ethernet systems using 802.3-style auto-negotiation and link training. This means teams can design for these devices without fundamentally changing the behavior of the endpoints or the protocol stack.


## Monitoring Mode: Diagnosing the Channel When Deeper Insight Is Needed


During design validation, manufacturing, and troubleshooting, engineers may need a more detailed view of the physical channel. Monitoring mode provides these deeper diagnostics.


#### Time-Domain Diagnostics


Time-domain diagnostics can characterize the channel’s step response and help identify physical connectivity issues. A known pattern, such as a jitter pattern or a specific PRBS pattern, is transmitted by the link partner. Smart Redrivers capture the resulting signal through on-chip analog-to-digital conversion, and firmware processes the data to determine the channel’s time-domain behavior.


This information can help teams establish baseline CTLE and VGA settings based on measured insertion loss. It can also help identify discontinuities during manufacturing or isolate a physical channel problem during system bring-up.


#### Eye Monitoring


Eye monitoring uses a similar sampling approach to reconstruct the eye from a known pattern. The resulting view provides another way to understand signal quality and margin on the link.


Together, time-domain and eye-monitoring capabilities give engineers more than a pass/fail result. They provide diagnostic information that can help connect a system symptom to a physical cause and reduce the time required to validate or troubleshoot a high-speed design.


## From Smart Devices to System-Level Visibility With COSMOS


Device-level intelligence is most valuable when it can be accessed consistently across a large deployment. AI infrastructure may contain hundreds or thousands of high-speed links, each with its own channel characteristics and operating conditions. Manually inspecting each link is not a scalable management strategy.


[COSMOS](https://www.asteralabs.com/products/cosmos/) provides a unified software environment for configuring, monitoring, and diagnosing Astera Labs connectivity devices. For Aries and Taurus Smart Redrivers, that environment can expose link-health indicators, equalization behavior, channel diagnostics, and device telemetry through a common management workflow.


This creates a path from isolated device data to fleet-level observability. Platform teams can establish repeatable validation procedures, monitor deployed systems, and accelerate root-cause analysis when a link behaves unexpectedly.


## The Next Generation of Redrivers Must Be Intelligent


As AI infrastructure moves to higher speeds and denser system architectures, link reliability cannot depend on fixed assumptions made during initial calibration. Channels change with temperature. Designs vary across boards and cables. And when a link begins to degrade, platform teams need visibility before the problem becomes an outage or a difficult-to-reproduce field failure.
